content:
The Cabinet Member noted the report which is

Tim Forrester, Solent Transport Manager/Future
Transport Zone Programme Manager gave a presentation on the Solent
Transport Programme.
 
Sub Regional Transport Model
This is currently managed by Hampshire County
Council, with Solent Transport providing oversight to ensure it
meets the wider region's needs.  Work is
underway to review best practice from other combined authorities
and to develop a scoping document and specification for
procurement.  The existing model uses
2019 data, so a short-term update is needed to make it fit for
purpose, while a longer-term approach will be developed by the new
combined authority, including consultation of future funding.
 
Integrated Ticketing
Work on integrated ticketing is at an early
stage and aims to establish the current position, barriers, and
future options for the region.  It is
seen as essential for the new combined authority, supporting
behaviour change and easier access across transport modes,
including buses, micromobility, ferries and trains, although
aligning different operators and regulatory frameworks would be
challenging.
 
There was a discussion on how integrated
ticketing could include ferry services, particularly for
pedestrians travelling to and from the Isle of Wight for essential
journeys such as healthcare.  It was
noted that ferry operators are not currently regulated in the same
way as other providers, but existing disruption agreements and
ongoing engagement with operators may provide a basis for future
integration.  The committee recognised
that developing a regional integrated ticketing offer would be
complex due to different operators, contracts, concessionary fares,
fare caps and local policies, and that the first step would be to
define the scope and customer requirements.
 
Micromobility
The success of the Solent micromobility
programme, currently managed by Solent Transport and operated by
Voi, was highlighted.  The scheme
includes over 2,500 vehicles, with more than 600 parking bays and
had delivered over 6 million rides, with survey data indicating a
34% shift from private car and taxi use.  It was noted that the scheme was regarded as best
practice nationally, supported by strong contract management, close
partnership working with Voi, high parking compliance, proactive
safety and enforcement measures, and plans to expand access so that
micromobility is available within a short walk of users.
 
The committee discussed safety, enforcement
and regulation around micromobility, particularly the distinction
between regulated Voi e-scooters/e-bikes and privately owned
vehicles.  Members noted concerns about
speeding, pavement use, anti-social behaviour and misuse such as
riding two-up, while recognising that the Voi scheme provides a
useful alternative to car use and offers more control through speed
restrictions, geo-fencing, reporting and enforcement processes.
 
It was agreed that private e-scooters remain
the main concern due to limited regulation and public awareness,
and that further education, police enforcement and national
legislation were needed. 
 
The committee supported the
proposal to write to the Transport Minister, highlighting the
positive aspects of the Voi scheme while raising concerns about
private e-scooters and the need for clearer
regulation.[FT1]

1.   
Noted that Portsmouth City Council will seek to nominate
representatives to the voluntary /Joint Committee that will be
doing the preparatory work to prepare for LGR for the new SE
Hampshire Unitary authority.
2.   
Noted that at the time of writing this report it is not certain how
many representatives Portsmouth will need to appoint to this
voluntary / Joint Committee, but we are working on the
representation, as determined by MHCLG, of 8 seats/votes.
3a.      Agreed that delegated
authority be given to the Chief Executive, in consultation with the
Leader of the Council, to finalise the list of appointees to the
voluntary / Joint Committee once it is clear how many the Council
will need to appoint.
3b.      Delegated to the Chief
Executive, in consultation with the Leader of the Council, the
authority to approve (once drafted) the Terms of Reference and
Procedural Rules for the Voluntary Joint Committee and the
subsequent Joint Committee to be established in advance of and once
the Structural Changes Order has been made. If approved the City
Solicitor to be authorised to make any necessary changes to the
Council's Constitution if required.
4.   
Agreed that the position of Portsmouth City Council, as is, would
be to support the name of the new unitary authority to be
"Portsmouth & South East Hampshire….." with a fallback
that the name must include Portsmouth.
5.   
Agreed that the new authority should have 14 wards, with three
councillors for each ward, covering the existing Portsmouth City
Council area.
6.   
Agreed that Charter Trustee route be used to secure City status and
civic and ceremonial matters for Portsmouth.
topline: The Portsmouth City Council has decided to nominate representatives, finalize appointees, support the name of the new unitary authority, determine wards and councillors, and secure City status for Portsmouth.

enquiries:

has adopted detailed guidance which it applies to proposals for
HMOs and applicants are expected to comply with this
guidance.

to:
(i)     
invest surplus funds in accordance with the approved Annual
Investment Strategy
(ii)    
borrow to finance short term cash deficits and capital payments
from any reputable source within the authorised limit for external
debt of £1,108m
(iii)   
reschedule debt to even the maturity profile or to achieve revenue
savings; and
(iv)  
buy and sell foreign currency, and to purchase hedging instruments
including forward purchases, forward options, and foreign exchange
rate swaps to mitigate the foreign exchange risks associated with
some contracts that are either priced in foreign currencies or
where the price is indexed against foreign currency exchange
rates.
6.             
Agree that the Director of Finance and Resources (Section 151
Officer) has the power to delegate treasury management operations
to relevant staff.
7.             
Agree that the Chief Executive, the Leader of the City Council and
the Chair of the Governance and Audit and Standards Committee be
informed of any material variances from the Treasury Management
Policy when they become apparent, and that the Leader of the City
Council be consulted on remedial action (paragraph 1.2.4 of
Treasury Management Policy Statement).
topline: The council has decided to approve the Treasury Management Policy Statement for 2026/27, setting investment and borrowing limits and delegation of authority.
